decision_reason: The assigned hls-project repository is an architecture/documentation map of the Harmonized Landsat Sentinel project, not the HLS processing software. Its README explicitly describes the separate repositories that contain the containers, utilities, and orchestration code. This repository contains only README/docs, and no root source license was found; the inventory's MIT label is not a direct grant. Reject this URL as a project index rather than an independent software product or source repository.

government_provenance.note: The exact README maps components used by the NASA Harmonized Landsat Sentinel (HLS) project and links the HLS product landing page; it identifies this repository's limited role as the project architecture map.

public_source.note: The repository contains only README.md and docs; the executable HLS containers, utilities, and orchestration are in separately linked repositories. This assigned URL is not the public source for the software it describes.

eligible_license.note: No LICENSE/COPYING grant is present at the repository root or in its visible file listing. The source inventory's MIT label is metadata only and cannot establish a grant for this repository or the linked HLS components.

primary_evidence.note: The README calls this an overview/map of a potentially large, multi-repository project and points to actual processing software in other repositories. It is documentation/index material, not a standalone HLS software product.

status_note: Reject the assigned URL as project-index documentation, not an executable product or canonical source. The README links many independently versioned component repositories; they must be reviewed individually before any component-level admission. GitHub shows a v1.0 README release in 2023, but that does not convert this map into the HLS processor or supply the missing repo license.

decision_reason: NASA's official catalog identifies ASSESS as an open-source application being developed to help the Department of Homeland Security identify applicable standards and links directly to this public repository. The README provides API-server, Elasticsearch, Redis, Docker Compose, and test guidance. However, no actual LICENSE/COPYING grant exists in the repository tree despite the inventory's Apache-2.0 label; the NASA catalog's release-type label is not a code license. The repository is also quiet since 2024, with no verified versioned release or current deployment/support signal. Hold pending an eligible grant and exact product lifecycle evidence.

government_provenance.note: NASA's exact product record describes ASSESS as an AI/ML application for the Department of Homeland Security and its Download Now link resolves to the reviewed nasa-jpl/ASSESS repository.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes API and ML source, Docker Compose configuration, and README setup/testing instructions without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The root file listing and recursive repository tree contain no LICENSE, COPYING, or other code grant. NASA's catalog identifies release type as Open Source and the inventory says Apache-2.0, but neither is the exact repository license text; no eligible grant is established.

primary_evidence.note: The repository documents an API application and Docker-based startup, while NASA's product record describes development for DHS. No versioned release or current product-specific operational/support evidence was verified; GitHub reports the last push as 2024-02-01.

decision_reason: The assigned nasa-jpl/LiveView URL now resolves to the canonical nasa-jpl/FlightView repository, whose README identifies the software as LiveView (aka FlightView), a real-time imaging-spectrometer data display used in JPL instrument integration/test and aircraft flight operations. The README names the JPL AVIRIS lab and a JPL maintainer, gives system requirements and installation-documentation links, and cites the exact LiveView co-verification paper. Source is public and actively maintained with substantive 2026 code changes. The exact GPL-3.0 grant is OSI-approved; the first grant-bearing code availability is 2018. Treat LiveView and FlightView as one product identity, not separate entries.

government_provenance.note: The canonical first-party repository README attributes the software to the Jet Propulsion Laboratory AVIRIS lab, gives a jpl.nasa.gov maintainer contact, and documents use in JPL instrument integration/test and aircraft flight operations, including AVIRIS and EMIT instruments.

public_source.note: The assigned old LiveView URL resolves to this public canonical repository, which exposes C++/Qt application and backend source, build files, documentation, and history without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The exact root license is GNU GPL version 3, an OSI-approved license. It applies to the repository-authored LiveView/FlightView source; CUDA, Qt, QCustomPlot, and other dependencies retain their own licenses/requirements.

primary_evidence.note: The exact README defines LiveView/FlightView as a real-time imaging-spectrometer viewer; documents high-rate acquisition, aircraft/instrument operations and named instrument families; gives system requirements and installation-documentation directions; and links the exact LiveView publication. Recent 2026 code commits support current maintenance.

product_identity: LiveView (also called FlightView), the real-time data-acquisition display and visualization application for imaging spectrometers; the old LiveView URL redirects to the canonical FlightView repository
agency: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), AVIRIS laboratory
geography: United States federal laboratory and aircraft instrument operations; the software handles imaging-spectrometer data for NASA/JPL instruments
license: GNU General Public License v3.0 (OSI-approved) for repository-authored code; third-party components retain separate licenses
status_note: Active. The current FlightView repo's README identifies JPL/AVIRIS authorship, operations use, installation documentation, and exact project name; the cited paper is specifically titled 'LiveView and P2serialcmds Co-Verification Software for NGIS and Embedded MPSoC Instrument Avionics' and identifies NASA/JPL/Caltech. The first grant-bearing commit is 53f984ebe20941ace1c9d90749047d2e286d0ccb (2018-04-18), which adds LICENSE.md with GPL-3.0 while application source was already in the repository. Do not backdate the open-source year to the README's 2014 authorship date. Repository has substantive source changes in February–June 2026. LiveView/FlightView is one family/product.

decision_reason: NASA's official catalog identifies PeTaL as an open-source tool/framework and its Download Now link points to this exact React front-end repository. The README labels PeTaL 0.4 and provides frontend start/deployment instructions; related API/database and Labeller repositories also publicly carry the Unlicense. However, the assigned repository is only the frontend of a three-repository service family, required backend/API/data/model parity and current support are not established by the stale component histories, and the family-wide earliest complete grant-bearing release year is not verified. The current GitHub Pages demo and NASA catalog listing do not by themselves demonstrate a currently operational backend or current exact source parity. Hold for a family-level current deployment/use and year crosswalk; do not list the frontend as a distinct product.

government_provenance.note: NASA's official software catalog names the Periodic Table of Life as a NASA open-source product and its Download Now link resolves to this exact PeTaL repository. The exact README describes the PeTaL project and its linked service-family repositories.

public_source.note: The public React frontend repository and its README are readable without credentials. The README links the separate public API/database and Labeller repositories required by the product family.

eligible_license.note: The actual frontend LICENSE text is the Unlicense, an OSI-approved public-domain dedication. The linked PeTaL-db and PeTaL-labeller repositories also currently expose actual Unlicense text for their authored source. README explicitly says AskNature datasets are not included because of property rights; the code grant is not claimed for that external data.

primary_evidence.note: The official NASA catalog and README support the product identity; the README documents PeTaL 0.4 and frontend setup, while linked backend/database and Labeller repos include additional setup guidance. But the assigned repo is only the React frontend, no family-wide first licensed-source year or current service/source parity has been confirmed, and the related service components are quiet (frontend last pushed 2023-11; database 2024-05; Labeller 2021-11). A current HTTP 200 from the static demo does not establish a working API/backend.
